entries.plain_meaning: Universal quantification: states that a geometric property holds for every choice of objects of the given types.
entries.formal_semantics: Dependent Pi-type binder Π (x : A), P x in Lean 4 / Coq; proof is a function mapping any witness x : A to a proof of P x.
entries.example_snippet: ∀ (a b : Point) (AB : Line), distinctPointsOnLine a b AB → ...
entries.geometor_equivalent: Function parameters on @proposition def prop_name(model: Model, a: Point, b: Point)

entries.plain_meaning: Existential quantification: asserts that a new geometric point, line, or circle can be constructed satisfying given conditions.
entries.formal_semantics: Inductive proposition Exists (λ x : A => P x) in Prop; eliminated via obtain / destruct / euclid_apply to introduce a fresh witness.
entries.geometor_equivalent: Explicit witness returned by model.intersect(...) or model.construct_line(...)

entries.plain_meaning: Logical implication ('if P then Q') or function arrow ('takes type A, returns type B'); right-associative.
entries.formal_semantics: Non-dependent special case of Π (_ : P), Q under Curry-Howard propositions-as-types.
entries.example_snippet: a ≠ b → Col A B C → Bet A B C ∨ Bet B C A ∨ Bet C A B
entries.geometor_equivalent: Precondition guards in Given(...) -> assertions in Demonstrate(...)

entries.plain_meaning: Logical equivalence: both directions P → Q and Q → P hold, allowing rewrite substitution.
entries.formal_semantics: Structure Iff P Q bundling mp : P → Q and mpr : Q → P; usable directly by rw / simp.
entries.example_snippet: ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π / 2 ↔ dist p₁ p₃ ^ 2 = dist p₁ p₂ ^ 2 + dist p₃ p₂ ^ 2
entries.geometor_equivalent: zero_test(lhs - rhs) equivalence between algebraic invariants

entries.plain_meaning: Logical conjunction: both geometric conditions hold simultaneously.
entries.formal_semantics: Product structure And P Q with projections .left (.1) and .right (.2); unpacked in GeoCoq by spliter.
entries.example_snippet: Bet A M B /\ Cong A M M B
entries.geometor_equivalent: Sequential assertions model.assert_equal(...); model.assert_perpendicular(...)

entries.plain_meaning: Logical disjunction: at least one of two geometric configurations holds (e.g., case split on point order).
entries.formal_semantics: Sum inductive Or P Q with constructors Or.inl and Or.inr.
entries.example_snippet: a.onLine L ∨ ¬(a.onLine L)
entries.geometor_equivalent: Selector branch selection in model.intersect(..., side_of=...)

entries.plain_meaning: Logical negation: states that a configuration is impossible (e.g., ~ Col A B C means non-collinear).
entries.formal_semantics: Defined constructively as P → False.
entries.example_snippet: ~ Col A B C -> exists X, Cong X A X B /\ Cong X B X C
entries.geometor_equivalent: not zero_test(signed_area2(a, b, c)) non-degeneracy check

entries.plain_meaning: Point or line distinctness precondition required to span a unique line or non-degenerate circle.
entries.formal_semantics: Shorthand for ¬(x = y), i.e. (x = y) → False (written x <> y in Coq).
entries.example_snippet: (hne : p₁ ≠ p₂)
entries.geometor_equivalent: quadrance(p1, p2) != 0 validated inside Model.construct_line / construct_circle

entries.plain_meaning: Declares an ambient space type V that Lean infers automatically from later arguments without making the user pass V by hand.
entries.formal_semantics: Curly braces {...} mark an implicit Pi-binder solved by unification; Type* expands to Sort (u + 1) for fresh universe u.
entries.example_snippet: variable {V : Type*} {P : Type*}
entries.geometor_equivalent: Python generic type annotations / ambient 2D SymPy coordinate domain

entries.pronunciation: typeclass instance: P is a normed affine torsor over vector space V
entries.plain_meaning: Equips points P with origin-free subtraction (producing a vector in V) and vector translation (producing a point in P) compatible with metric distance.
entries.formal_semantics: Square brackets [...] trigger Lean's backward typeclass synthesis for AddTorsor V P + dist_eq_norm_vsub.
entries.example_snippet: [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [MetricSpace P] [NormedAddTorsor V P]
entries.geometor_equivalent: spg.Point2D affine arithmetic paired with geometor.model.invariants.quadrance

entries.plain_meaning: Real non-negative length assigned to the segment between points a and b in Formal System E.
entries.formal_semantics: Custom Lean 4 notation (Relations.lean) mapping Point × Point → ℝ with symmetry |(a─b)| = |(b─a)| and positivity |(a─b)| > 0 ↔ a ≠ b.
entries.geometor_equivalent: quadrance(a, b) (rational squared length) or spg.Segment(a, b).length

entries.pronunciation: measure of rectilinear angle a-b-c at vertex b
entries.plain_meaning: Real measure of the interior angle formed by rays ba and bc, bounded between 0 and two RightAngles.
entries.formal_semantics: System E metric sort map Angle.ofPoints a b c : ℝ obeying diagrammatic ray-splitting additivity when d lies between a and c.
entries.geometor_equivalent: vertex_spread(a, b, c) + vertex_dot_sign(a, b, c) in geometor.model

entries.pronunciation: area of triangle a b c
entries.plain_meaning: Unsigned real area of triangle abc in System E, additive under interior cevians and invariant under SAS congruence.
entries.formal_semantics: Function Triangle.area (Triangle.ofPoints a b c) : ℝ; equals 0 when a, b, c are collinear.
entries.geometor_equivalent: abs(signed_area2(a, b, c)) / 2 or model.assert_area_equal(poly1, poly2)

entries.plain_meaning: Euclid's Postulate 4 unit of angular measure (all right angles are equal), avoiding transcendental π.
entries.formal_semantics: Positive real constant RightAngle : ℝ in SystemE/Theory/Relations.lean; straight angle equals ∟ + ∟.
entries.geometor_equivalent: line_spread(l1, l2) == 1 or model.assert_perpendicular(l1, l2)

entries.pronunciation: points p and q lie on the same side of line L
entries.plain_meaning: Topological half-plane relation: neither p nor q lies on L, and segment pq does not intersect L.
entries.formal_semantics: Primitive diagrammatic predicate Point.sameSide p q L : Prop governed by Pasch/plane-separation axioms.
entries.example_snippet: p.sameSide q AB
entries.geometor_equivalent: side_of=(a, b, +1) selector in model.intersect(...)

entries.pronunciation: points p and q lie on opposite sides of line L
entries.plain_meaning: Topological separation: p and q lie off L and the open segment pq intersects L.
entries.formal_semantics: Defined in Relations.lean as ¬(p.onLine L) ∧ ¬(q.onLine L) ∧ ¬(p.sameSide q L).
entries.example_snippet: c.opposingSides d AB
entries.geometor_equivalent: side_of=(a, b, -1) selector in model.intersect(...)

entries.plain_meaning: Strict collinear order: point b lies on line ac strictly inside open segment (a, c).
entries.formal_semantics: In LeanEuclid: strict ternary predicate between a b c (implies a ≠ b, b ≠ c, ¬between b a c). In geometor.model: intersect(..., between=(a, c)) selects root with 0 < t < 1.
entries.example_snippet: m = model.intersect(l_ab, l_ef, between=(a, b), ID='M')
entries.geometor_equivalent: model.intersect(e1, e2, between=(p1, p2))

entries.pronunciation: apply Euclidean construction or proposition rule
entries.plain_meaning: Executes a compass-and-straightedge construction rule or prior proposition, introducing a fresh geometric object into context while discharging preconditions via SMT.
entries.formal_semantics: Lean 4 tactic macro in SystemE/Tactics/ translating context + negated precondition to SMT-LIB2 for Z3/CVC5.
entries.example_snippet: euclid_apply (Intersections.intersect_circles α β) as c
entries.geometor_equivalent: c = model.intersect(alpha, beta, side_of=(a, b, 1))

entries.plain_meaning: Internal trust-oracle axiom used by LeanEuclid whenever external Z3/CVC5 reports 'unsat', closing the Lean goal without a kernel proof term.
entries.formal_semantics: axiom SMT_VERIF (P : Prop) : P in SystemE/Meta/Smt/Solver.lean:44-55 (explicitly marked 'Dangerous!').
entries.example_snippet: private axiom SMT_VERIF (P : Prop) : P
entries.geometor_equivalent: Avoided in GEOMETOR: algebraic identities are reduced symbolically via SymPy ANP fields

entries.plain_meaning: Point B lies on the closed line segment AC (allowing B = A or B = C!).
entries.formal_semantics: Primitive ternary relation Bet : Tpoint -> Tpoint -> Tpoint -> Prop in Tarski_neutral_dimensionless; Col A B C := Bet A B C \/ Bet B C A \/ Bet C A B.
entries.example_snippet: assert (Bet A M B) by eBetween.
entries.geometor_equivalent: zero_test(signed_area2(a, b, c)) and dot-product parameter 0 <= t <= 1

entries.plain_meaning: The distance from A to B equals the distance from C to D, stated purely on four points without numbers or segment objects.
entries.formal_semantics: Primitive quaternary relation Cong : Tpoint -> Tpoint -> Tpoint -> Tpoint -> Prop (in AG/Newclid: cong A B C D).
entries.example_snippet: Cong A B C D
entries.geometor_equivalent: model.assert_equal((a, b), (c, d))  # zero_test(quadrance(a, b) - quadrance(c, d))

entries.plain_meaning: Tarski's angle-free replacement for SAS triangle congruence: if collinear triples (A,B,C) and (A',B',C') have matching base segments and matching legs to apexes D, D', then the 5th segments CD and C'D' are congruent.
entries.formal_semantics: FSC A B C D A' B' C' D' := Col A B C /\ Cong A B A' B' /\ Cong B C B' C' /\ Cong A D A' D' /\ Cong B D B' D'.
entries.example_snippet: Lemma l4_16 : FSC A B C D A' B' C' D' -> A <> B -> Cong C D C' D'.
entries.geometor_equivalent: Stewart's / Triple-Quad polynomial determination of Q(C, D) from collinear base quadrances

entries.pronunciation: Tarski right angle via midpoint reflection
entries.plain_meaning: Angle ABC is a right angle iff reflecting C across B to C' makes A equidistant from C and C'—defining 90 degrees with zero angle primitives!
entries.formal_semantics: Definition Per A B C := exists C', Midpoint B C C' /\ Cong A C A C' (Ch08_orthogonality.v).
entries.example_snippet: Per A B C <-> exists C', Midpoint B C C' /\ Cong A C A C'
entries.geometor_equivalent: vertex_spread(a, b, c) == 1 or model.assert_perpendicular((a, b), (b, c), at=b)

entries.pronunciation: one side / two sides of line AB
entries.plain_meaning: TS A B P Q means segment PQ crosses line AB; OS A B P Q means P and Q lie on the same side because both lie opposite some witness R.
entries.formal_semantics: TS A B P Q := ~Col P A B /\ ~Col Q A B /\ exists T, Col T A B /\ Bet P T Q; OS A B P Q := exists R, TS A B P R /\ TS A B Q R.
entries.example_snippet: OS A B P Q -> TS A B Q R -> TS A B P R
entries.geometor_equivalent: sp.sign(signed_area2(a, b, p) * signed_area2(a, b, q)) == +1 (OS) or -1 (TS)

entries.plain_meaning: Par_strict A B C D means coplanar lines AB and CD never meet; Par A B C D allows either strict parallelism or collinear coincidence.
entries.formal_semantics: Par A B C D := Par_strict A B C D \/ (A <> B /\ C <> D /\ Col A C D /\ Col B C D) (Ch12_parallel.v).
entries.example_snippet: Par A B C D
entries.geometor_equivalent: model.assert_parallel(l1, l2)  # line_spread(l1, l2) == 0

entries.pronunciation: same open ray from vertex P
entries.plain_meaning: Points A and B are distinct from P and lie on the same half-ray emanating from P (either Bet P A B or Bet P B A).
entries.formal_semantics: Out P A B := A <> P /\ B <> P /\ (Bet P A B \/ Bet P B A) (Ch06_out_lines.v).
entries.example_snippet: Out P A B
entries.geometor_equivalent: on_ray=(p, a) selector in model.intersect(...)

entries.pronunciation: certified Coq reflection tactic for collinearity / congruence
entries.plain_meaning: Automatically proves collinearity or congruence goals by reifying context facts into an algebraic data structure inside Coq and running a verified decision procedure.
entries.formal_semantics: Kernel-checked computational reflection tactics in Meta_theory/ / Tactics/Coinc/—zero external trust axioms!
entries.example_snippet: intros; spliter; ColR.
entries.geometor_equivalent: ExactDDARSolver / zero_test(signed_area2(...)) inside SymPy

entries.plain_meaning: Subtracts base point p₂ from target point p₁ to produce the displacement vector from p₂ to p₁ (note: you can subtract points, never add points!).
entries.formal_semantics: VSub.vsub : P → P → V; p₁ -ᵥ p₂ represents the vector v such that v +ᵥ p₂ = p₁.
entries.example_snippet: dist p₁ p₂ = ‖p₁ -ᵥ p₂‖
entries.geometor_equivalent: sp.Matrix([p1.x - p2.x, p1.y - p2.y])

entries.plain_meaning: Translates point p by displacement vector v to yield a new point in P.
entries.formal_semantics: VAdd.vadd : V → P → P satisfying 0 +ᵥ p = p and (v₁ + v₂) +ᵥ p = v₁ +ᵥ (v₂ +ᵥ p).
entries.example_snippet: v +ᵥ p
entries.geometor_equivalent: spg.Point2D(p.x + vx, p.y + vy)

entries.pronunciation: real inner (dot) product of vectors x and y
entries.plain_meaning: Measures orthogonal projection and cosine similarity between displacement vectors in V.
entries.formal_semantics: Scoped RealInnerProductSpace notation for inner ℝ x y : ℝ.
entries.example_snippet: ⟪p₁ -ᵥ p₂, p₃ -ᵥ p₂⟫ = 0

entries.pronunciation: affine span (line) over ℝ through p₁ and p₂
entries.plain_meaning: The 1-dimensional affine subspace spanned by points p₁ and p₂ (degenerating to a singleton {p₁} if p₁ = p₂).
entries.formal_semantics: Notation for affineSpan ℝ ({p₁, p₂} : Set P) : AffineSubspace ℝ P.
entries.example_snippet: p₃ ∈ line[ℝ, p₁, p₂]
entries.geometor_equivalent: model.construct_line(p1, p2)

entries.plain_meaning: Given a vector subspace (such as a line's direction), returns the subspace of all vectors perpendicular to it.
entries.formal_semantics: Submodule.orthogonal K : Submodule ℝ V; used with mk' p s.directionᗮ to build perpendicular affine subspaces of codimension k.
entries.example_snippet: AffineSubspace.mk' p s.directionᗮ
entries.geometor_equivalent: Normal direction (-b, a) of line ax + by + c = 0

entries.plain_meaning: Classical unoriented angle at middle vertex p₂ in any inner-product dimension; returns junk value π/2 if p₁ = p₂ or p₃ = p₂.
entries.formal_semantics: InnerProductGeometry.angle (p₁ -ᵥ p₂) (p₃ -ᵥ p₂) := Real.arccos (⟪u, v⟫ / (‖u‖ * ‖v‖)) ∈ [0, π].
entries.example_snippet: ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π / 2
entries.geometor_equivalent: vertex_spread(p1, p2, p3) + vertex_dot_sign(p1, p2, p3) (avoids transcendental arccos!)

entries.plain_meaning: Counterclockwise angle from ray yx to ray yz in ℝ/(2πℤ); multiplying by 2 gives (2 : ℤ) • ∡ x y z, encoding directed line angles modulo π!
entries.formal_semantics: Orientation.oangle (x -ᵥ y) (z -ᵥ y) : Real.Angle (= QuotientAddGroup.Quotient (2πℤ)).
entries.example_snippet: cospherical {p₁, p₂, p₃, p₄} ↔ (2 : ℤ) • ∡ p₁ p₂ p₄ = (2 : ℤ) • ∡ p₁ p₃ p₄
entries.geometor_equivalent: eqangle modulo π / rational spread + signed orientation

entries.pronunciation: power / pole / polar of an n-dimensional Euclidean sphere
entries.plain_meaning: Clean n-dimensional sphere API: s.power p = dist(p, s.center)^2 - s.radius^2, enabling 1-line proofs of intersecting chords and La Hire's pole-polar reciprocity.
entries.formal_semantics: Defined in Mathlib/Geometry/Euclidean/Sphere/{Power,SecondInter,PolePolar}.lean over arbitrary InnerProductSpace ℝ V.
entries.example_snippet: s.power p = dist p s.center ^ 2 - s.radius ^ 2
entries.geometor_equivalent: quadrance(p, c) - r_quad (planned geometor.model.inversion.circle_power)

entries.plain_meaning: Splits the ordered construction clauses on the left from the target predicate goal(s) on the right.
entries.formal_semantics: Parsed by Problem.from_txt (problem.py:138); Newclid extends RHS to semicolon-separated multi-goals.
entries.example_snippet: a b c = triangle a b c; h = orthocenter h a b c ? perp a h b c
entries.geometor_equivalent: Transition from Construct(...) to Demonstrate(...) inside @proposition

entries.plain_meaning: Separates sequential point-introducing clauses in a problem string; also separates plevel groups in Line 4 of defs.txt (with a silent-drop bug in AG if unprefixed!).
entries.formal_semantics: Splits Problem premises into ordered Clause objects (problem.py:140).
entries.example_snippet: a b = segment a b; c = on_circle c a b, on_circle c b a
entries.geometor_equivalent: Sequential Python statements appending Step entries to Model.steps

entries.plain_meaning: Inside a single clause x = locus1, locus2, constrains point x to lie on both loci simultaneously (computing their intersection while puncturing pre-existing points via HoleCircle).
entries.formal_semantics: Evaluated in numericals.py:1297-1323 (nm.reduce) and injected conjunctively into Graph.add_clause.
entries.example_snippet: h = on_tline h b a c, on_tline h c a b
entries.geometor_equivalent: h = model.intersect(alt_b, alt_c, other_than=...)

entries.plain_meaning: In Newclid problem strings, separates given base clauses from agent-proposed auxiliary constructions before '?'. (In kingdon/galgebra Python code, A | B is the metric inner product.)
entries.formal_semantics: Parsed in newclid/jgex/formulation.py:92-100 into base clauses vs auxiliary_clauses.
entries.example_snippet: a b c = triangle; h = on_tline b a c, on_tline c a b | e = on_line a c, on_line b h ? perp a h b c
entries.geometor_equivalent: with model.subconstruction('aux'): ... auxiliary witness introduction

entries.plain_meaning: Hardcodes floating-point (x, y) coordinates onto a free point in imo_ag_30.txt so random numerical sketching lands in the intended acute/obtuse topological branch.
entries.formal_semantics: Parsed in Clause.from_txt (alphageometry/problem.py:88-91) via float(x), float(y).
entries.geometor_equivalent: Exact symbolic seed coordinates model.set_point(sp.Rational(...), ...)

entries.plain_meaning: The counterclockwise angle required to rotate line AB onto line CD equals the angle from line EF to line GH modulo 180 degrees.
entries.formal_semantics: d(CD) - d(AB) ≡ d(GH) - d(EF) (mod π) in AngleTable (ar.py:591-656); unifies inscribed angles without case splits, at the cost of conflating internal and external angle bisectors!
entries.example_snippet: eqangle P A P B Q A Q B
entries.geometor_equivalent: model.assert_spread_equal(...) (spread s = sin^2 θ is also π-periodic!)

entries.plain_meaning: The ratio of segment lengths |AB| / |CD| equals |EF| / |GH|.
entries.formal_semantics: Encoded in RatioTable as log|AB| - log|CD| - log|EF| + log|GH| = 0 (ar.py:576-586).
entries.example_snippet: eqratio P A P C P D P B
entries.geometor_equivalent: zero_test(quadrance(p, a) * quadrance(p, b) - quadrance(p, c) * quadrance(p, d))

entries.pronunciation: constant rational segment ratio (buggy in AlphaGeometry!)
entries.plain_meaning: States |AB| / |CD| = m / n. In AlphaGeometry ar.py:570-574, buggy add_eq2 adds m*log|AB| - n*log|CD| = 0 (|AB|^m = |CD|^n!); fixed in Newclid via sp.log(m) - sp.log(n).
entries.formal_semantics: Intended: l(AB) - l(CD) = log(m/n). AlphaGeometry bug: m*l(AB) - n*l(CD) = 0.
entries.example_snippet: rconst m a a b 1 2
entries.geometor_equivalent: zero_test(quadrance(m, a) * 4 - quadrance(a, b) * 1)

entries.pronunciation: concyclic points (lie on a common circle)
entries.plain_meaning: Four or more points lie on a single circle, without needing to construct the circle's center first.
entries.formal_semantics: Merges points onto a gm.Circle node (graph.py:1317); linked to eqangle via inscribed-angle rules r03/r04.
entries.example_snippet: cyclic A B P Q
entries.geometor_equivalent: 4x4 Cayley-Menger /lifting determinant det([x_i, y_i, x_i^2+y_i^2, 1]) == 0

entries.plain_meaning: simtri means ΔABC and ΔPQR are directly similar (same clockwise orientation); simtri2 (simtrir in Newclid) means oppositely/reflectedly similar.
entries.formal_semantics: Checked via sameclock guard and expanded into 3 eqangle + 3 eqratio relations with reversed angle signs for simtri2 (graph.py:2350-2381).
entries.example_snippet: simtri2 H B A A B C
entries.geometor_equivalent: Equal spreads + opposite sign of signed_area2(a, b, c) * signed_area2(p, q, r)

entries.pronunciation: Chou-Gao-Zhang signed area of triangle ABC
entries.plain_meaning: Coordinate-free oriented area invariant: vanishes iff A, B, C are collinear; S_ABCD = S_ABC + S_ACD vanishes iff AB || CD; co-side ratio AB/CD = S_PAB/S_PCD eliminates intersections linearly!
entries.formal_semantics: Var.nm = 2 in JGEX Poly.java:1767 / Elim.trim_a; obeys Chasles identity S_ABC = S_PBC + S_APC + S_ABP.
entries.example_snippet: G(Y) = (S_UPQ * G(V) - S_VPQ * G(U)) / S_UPVQ
entries.geometor_equivalent: geometor.model.invariants.signed_area2(a, b, c)  # exact 2 * S_ABC

entries.plain_meaning: Coordinate-free metric invariant P_ABC = AB^2 + BC^2 - AC^2 (= 2 BA · BC) and 4-point P_ABCD = AB^2 + CD^2 - BC^2 - DA^2 (= 2 AC · BD); vanishes iff perpendicular!
entries.formal_semantics: Var.nm = 3 in JGEX Poly.java:1796 / Elim.trim_g; satisfies Jacobi identity P_ACHB + P_BAHC + P_CBAH = 0 (0-step orthocenter proof!).
entries.example_snippet: PERPENDICULAR A B B C <=> P_ABC = 0
entries.geometor_equivalent: quadrance(a, b) + quadrance(b, c) - quadrance(a, c)

entries.plain_meaning: Antisymmetric subspace spanning product: in plane-based 2D PGA it computes the MEET of two lines (l1 ^ l2 = point); in point-based 2D CGA it computes the JOIN (P1 ^ P2 ^ P3 = circle; P1 ^ P2 ^ ni = line)!
entries.formal_semantics: Grade-(k+l) part <A * B>_{k+l} of the geometric product (kingdon/operators.py:202, galgebra/mv.py:785).
entries.example_snippet: C_circ = P1 ^ P2 ^ P3  # 2D CGA circle through 3 points
entries.geometor_equivalent: model.intersect(l1, l2) (in PGA) or circumcircle / construct_line (in CGA)

entries.plain_meaning: Dual subspace intersection/join product (A* ^ B*)^{-*}: in plane-based 2D PGA, P1 & P2 JOINS two points into a line and (P1 & P2 & P3).e is their 3x3 collinearity determinant! (Missing in galgebra!)
entries.formal_semantics: Implemented in kingdon/operators.py:215-241 via Hodge dual of outer product.
entries.example_snippet: l_ab = A & B; pappus_zero = (P & Q & R).e
entries.geometor_equivalent: model.construct_line(a, b) and signed_area2(p, q, r)

entries.plain_meaning: Computes metric projections, orthogonality, quadrances, and circle power: in 2D PGA, (l | P) is the line through P perpendicular to l; in 2D CGA, -2*(P1 | P2) is quadrance |p1-p2|^2 and -2*(kappa | P) is Steiner power!
entries.formal_semantics: Grade |k - l| projection <A * B>_{|k-l|} (kingdon/operators.py:146; warning: galgebra returns 0 on grade-0 scalars!).
entries.example_snippet: l_bis = (A & B) | (A + B)  # 2D PGA perpendicular bisector
entries.geometor_equivalent: quadrance(p1, p2) / perpendicular construction

entries.pronunciation: versor sandwich product (kingdon) — WARNING: commutator in galgebra!
entries.plain_meaning: Applies any reflection, rotation, translation, or circle inversion uniformly to points, lines, or circles via ±V * X * ~V! (Critical trap: in galgebra, >> is 0.5*(AB - BA) commutator, NOT sandwich!)
entries.formal_semantics: In kingdon (operators.py:96-121): (-1)^{k*l} V * X * ~V for unit versor V*~V = 1.
entries.example_snippet: P_inv = norm_pt(C1.normalized() >> P)  # 2D CGA circle inversion!
entries.geometor_equivalent: Unified reflection / rotation / circle inversion transformation

entries.plain_meaning: Reverses the multiplication order of basis vectors in every blade (flipping signs of bivectors and trivectors); acts like Hermitian adjoint for rotors (R * ~R = 1).
entries.formal_semantics: Flips sign by (-1)^{k(k-1)/2} on grade-k blades (kingdon/operators.py:446).
entries.example_snippet: X3 = norm_pt(C_circ * ni * ~C_circ)  # 2D CGA circumcenter!
entries.geometor_equivalent: Conjugate / inverse orientation in versor composition

entries.plain_meaning: Converts between direct OPNS blades (where ^ is join) and dual IPNS blades (where ^ is meet): e.g., dualizing C = P1^P2^P3 gives grade-1 dual circle kappa = O - 0.5*r^2*ni. (Crashes in galgebra when I^2 = 0!)
entries.formal_semantics: kingdon auto-dispatches metric polarity x * I^{-1} when r=0 (CGA) and right Hodge complement when r>=1 (PGA).
entries.example_snippet: kappa = (P1 ^ P2 ^ P3).dual(); lam_rad = kappa1 - kappa2
entries.geometor_equivalent: Point-line projective duality / monic circle vector

entries.pronunciation: ideal line e0 (PGA) / conformal infinity ni & origin no (CGA)
entries.plain_meaning: Null basis vectors (squaring to 0) that linearize translations and circles: in 2D PGA, e0 is the line at infinity; in 2D CGA, ni represents infinity and no the origin with no | ni = -1.
entries.example_snippet: up = lambda x, y: x*e1 + y*e2 + sp.Rational(1, 2)*(x**2 + y**2)*ni + no
entries.geometor_equivalent: Homogeneous z=0 ideal locus / parabolic lifting x^2 + y^2

entries.pronunciation: 3D homogeneous cross product (unified Join and Meet)
entries.plain_meaning: In homogeneous coordinates [x, y, z], the 3D vector cross product u × v simultaneously computes the line joining two points AND the intersection point of two lines—including parallel lines meeting at z = 0!
entries.formal_semantics: Bilinear map CP^2 × CP^2 -> CP^2 in CindyJS GeoOps.js:156-202 (and geometor.pappus).
entries.example_snippet: P = cross(cross(A1, B2), cross(A2, B1));
entries.geometor_equivalent: sp.Matrix(u).cross(sp.Matrix(v)) in geometor.pappus

entries.plain_meaning: Given symmetric 3x3 point-conic matrix C (p^T C p = 0), C * p is the polar line of p, adj(C) is the division-free dual tangent conic, and adj(C) * l is the pole of line l!
entries.formal_semantics: List.adjoint3(C) = det(C) * C^{-1} over complex homogeneous coordinates (List.js:1386-1501).
entries.example_snippet: l_polar = C1 * p; p_pole = adjoint3(C1) * l;
entries.geometor_equivalent: C.adjugate() over exact SymPy Matrix(3, 3, ...)

entries.plain_meaning: Every Euclidean circle is simply a projective conic passing through I=(1, i, 0) and J=(1, -i, 0)! Perpendicularity is harmonic conjugacy wrt I, J, and Euclidean angle is (i/2) ln CR(A_inf, B_inf; I, J).
entries.formal_semantics: List.ii = [1, i, 0], List.jj = [1, -i, 0], List.fundDual = diag(1, 1, 0) in List.js:111-126.
entries.example_snippet: geoOps._helper.ConicBy5(el, a, b, List.ii, List.jj, p);
entries.geometor_equivalent: Algebraic unification of Euclidean metric and projective cross-ratio

entries.plain_meaning: Selects a deterministic intersection point from a quadratic line-circle or circle-circle step using exact sign of oriented area (side_of), dot-product order (between, beyond, on_ray), or known-point exclusion (other_than).
entries.formal_semantics: Evaluated in geometor.model.intersections.intersect (lines 382-620) without floating-point branch ambiguity.
entries.example_snippet: f = m.intersect(c_a, c_b, side_of=(a, b, 1), ID='F')
entries.geometor_equivalent: Native geometor.model.Model.intersect(..., side_of=(p1, p2, +1))

entries.plain_meaning: Exact polynomial squared distance (x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2 between two points, avoiding square roots so geometry stays inside the base number field.
entries.formal_semantics: Pure degree-2 polynomial invariant in geometor.model.invariants.quadrance / geometor.wildberger.
entries.example_snippet: q_ab = quadrance(a, b)  # exact SymPy Rational or ANP element
entries.geometor_equivalent: Native geometor.model.quadrance(p1, p2)

entries.pronunciation: Wildberger spread (rational squared sine between lines)
entries.plain_meaning: Exact rational invariant s(l1, l2) ∈ [0, 1] measuring line separation (= sin^2 θ): 0 for parallel lines, 1/2 for 45°, 3/4 for 60°, and 1 for perpendicular lines—with zero inverse trig functions!
entries.formal_semantics: (a1*b2 - a2*b1)^2 / ((a1^2 + b1^2)*(a2^2 + b2^2)) in geometor.model.invariants.line_spread.
entries.example_snippet: s = vertex_spread(b, a, f)  # sp.Rational(3, 4) for equilateral apex
entries.geometor_equivalent: Native geometor.model.line_spread / vertex_spread

entries.pronunciation: projective cross-ratio of four collinear points
entries.plain_meaning: Fundamental projective invariant preserved under central projection; equals -1 when (A, B; C, D) form a harmonic range (such as internal/external bisector feet or circle diameter + pole/inverse).
entries.formal_semantics: Signed ratio (AC * BD) / (BC * AD) (or (AC * BD) / (AD * BC) depending on pairing convention—explicitly audited across model vs pappus!).
entries.example_snippet: assert is_harmonic(r_neg, r_pos, p_inv, p)  # CR == -1
entries.geometor_equivalent: Native geometor.model.cross_ratio / is_harmonic

entries.pronunciation: exact rational algebraic number field Q(α)
entries.plain_meaning: Represents nested radicals (such as golden ratio φ or √3) as canonical modulo-minimal-polynomial elements in Q[α]/(m(α)), reducing multi-step radical expressions to 0 deterministically.
entries.formal_semantics: SymPy Polys AlgebraicField constructed via sp.primitive_element in geometor.model.algebra.
entries.example_snippet: K = sp.QQ.algebraic_field(sp.GoldenRatio)
entries.geometor_equivalent: Core canonicalizer inside geometor.model.algebra.zero_test

entries.pronunciation: Byrne inline coloured value-token (segment / wedge / polygon / circle)
entries.plain_meaning: Replaces symbolic vertex-letter pointers ('AB', '∠ABC', '△ABC') with miniature coloured geometric shapes (red, blue, yellow, black) set inline inside algebraic-logical equations, eliminating visual pointer-chasing!
entries.formal_semantics: Direct value-token binding (Pickering 1847 woodblocks; encoded as inline <svg> components with shared class hover listeners in Rougeux's c82.net/euclid).
entries.example_snippet: [red ━━] = [blue ━━],  [yellow ━━] = [blue ━━]  ∴  [red ━━] = [yellow ━━]
entries.geometor_equivalent: Bidirectional :g:`[ A B ]` <-> .euclid-graphic data-ref hover highlighting

entries.pronunciation: as A is to B, so is C to D (Oughtred-Byrne four-term proportion)
entries.plain_meaning: Four-term Eudoxian geometric proportion introduced by William Oughtred (1631) and used across Byrne Books V-VI with coloured ribbon/segment glyphs (including extreme & mean golden ratio [whole] : [blue] :: [blue] : [red]!).
entries.formal_semantics: Eudoxian equimultiple proportion Definition V.5 over geometric magnitudes.
entries.example_snippet: [red+blue ━━] : [blue ━━] :: [blue ━━] : [red ━━]  (Euclid VI.30 / φ)
entries.geometor_equivalent: eqratio / cross_ratio / geometor.divine golden proportion chains

entries.plain_meaning: Introduces each derived equation line in Byrne's vertical Proof block, paired with marginal proposition/axiom citations such as (I.4) or (Ax. 1).
entries.formal_semantics: Modus ponens inference marker introduced by Johann Rahn (1659) and standardized as vertical proof pseudocode in Byrne (1847).
entries.geometor_equivalent: model.assert_*(..., by='I.13') and conclude(...) in @proposition

entries.plain_meaning: Visually separates auxiliary loci introduced in the Construction block (dashed/dotted lines) from Given premise loci (solid lines) while multiplying 4 primary colors into ~12 distinct visual tokens.
entries.formal_semantics: Typographic modality distinguishing premise vs existential witness loci.
entries.example_snippet: Draw [red ╌╌╌] parallel to [black ━━]  (Byrne I.31 Construction)
entries.geometor_equivalent: classes=['guide'] / guide=True and model.subconstruction(...)

entries.plain_meaning: Synthesizes classical symbolic pointer precision (:g:`A`, :g:`[ A B ]`, :g:`( A B )`) with Byrne/Rougeux zero-dereference visual perception via live two-way CSS/DOM data-ref hover illumination on inline .euclid-graphic SVGs.
entries.formal_semantics: Sphinx role in photon_platform.publish.roles.geometry emitting <span class='geometor-ref' data-ref='...'>.
entries.example_snippet: Join poles :g:`F` and :g:`E` along bisector :g:`[ E F ]`.
entries.geometor_equivalent: Native GEOMETOR / Digital Scriptorium standard

entries.pronunciation: structured Given / Construct / Demonstrate proposition block
entries.plain_meaning: Formalizes Proclus's 6-part Euclidean anatomy and Byrne's 4-block typographic layout (Given -> To Prove -> Construction -> Proof) as executable, machine-verified Python proof traces.
entries.formal_semantics: Decorator in geometor.model.proof recording structured Step phases and algebraic assertions.
entries.example_snippet:
@proposition('I.1')
def equilateral_triangle(m: Model): ...
entries.geometor_equivalent: Native geometor.model.proof.@proposition
